messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Shiny 0.9.0
parts:
Hi all,


We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.9.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.8.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:


   if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')

   devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')


New Shiny Application Layout


We provided the sidebar layout and tabsets in the past. Shiny 0.9.0 introduced a few new layout and navigation functions to


  1. make it easier to create custom page layouts using the Bootstrap grid system

  2. provide navigation containers for creating larger applications (Navbars and Navlists)


The functions fluidRow() and column() can be used in the Bootstrap grid system to create rows and columns, respectively. The navlistPanel() function may be a good alternative to tabsetPanel(). A navlist presents the various components as a sidebar list rather than using tabs. You can see details in the new layout guide.


Selectize.js Integration


The JavaScript library selectize.js provides a much more flexible interface compared to the basic select input. It allows us to type and search in the options, use placeholders, control the number of options/items to show/select, and so on. We have integrated selectize.js in shiny, and selectize input can be created via the new function selectizeInput(). Note the original selectInput() function uses selectize by default; you can revert back by selectInput(..., selectize = FALSE).


Please check out this example to see a subset of features of the selectize input. There is also an example comparing the select and selectize input.


Enhancements of DataTables Support


We can pass literal JavaScript code via the options argument in renderDataTable() now. This makes it much easier to use DataTable plugin’s and callback functions. More DataTables options are respected on the R side, including bPaginate, iDisplayLength, bSearchable, bFilter, and so on. It is also possible to filter numeric columns with lower/upper limits.


There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS file. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.


Thanks for your support -- we look forward to hearing from you!


-- The Shiny team

Hi Dmitri, I just pushed a fix for the matrixInput issue. If you install the latest shinyIncubator, it should work.

library(devtools) # Make sure you have version >=1.4
install_github('rstudio/shiny-incubator')

# You can run the example app with:
appdir <- system.file('examples', 'matrixinput', package='shinyIncubator')
runApp(appdir)

-Winston

Hi all,


We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.9.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.8.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:


   if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')

   devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')


New Shiny Application Layout


We provided the sidebar layout and tabsets in the past. Shiny 0.9.0 introduced a few new layout and navigation functions to


  1. make it easier to create custom page layouts using the Bootstrap grid system

  2. provide navigation containers for creating larger applications (Navbars and Navlists)


The functions fluidRow() and column() can be used in the Bootstrap grid system to create rows and columns, respectively. The navlistPanel() function may be a good alternative to tabsetPanel(). A navlist presents the various components as a sidebar list rather than using tabs. You can see details in the new layout guide.


Selectize.js Integration


The JavaScript library selectize.js provides a much more flexible interface compared to the basic select input. It allows us to type and search in the options, use placeholders, control the number of options/items to show/select, and so on. We have integrated selectize.js in shiny, and selectize input can be created via the new function selectizeInput(). Note the original selectInput() function uses selectize by default; you can revert back by selectInput(..., selectize = FALSE).


Please check out this example to see a subset of features of the selectize input. There is also an example comparing the select and selectize input.
